quotes.hub: Samuel, we're about to put more money behind beta and D1 and D7 are what we get judged on, so I want one straight answer on what we actually say to players. The PN sheet says six are Ready and I don't trust that. Take every row on the PNs Beta tab plus every ask for a new phone message that's been filed on a ticket or a card up to today, and make a call on each one using the message rule doc. Put it in one sheet in your Drive folder, one row per message: Message, Ticket, Call, What's missing, Audience, Final headline, String change. Next to it a one-page note for the team: start with D1 and D7 for the Sep 15 cohort week from the warehouse, iOS and Android separately, then the lapsed reminders the client schedules day by day, and anything the client already schedules that's still a Hold and why. I made tickets for the sheet rows under DES-314 and people added their asks there. Leave the call as a comment on each ticket and move the ticket to match. Anything with no ticket gets one, but don't make a second one for something that already has a ticket under whatever name. Every Go goes on a checklist on our push notifications card so Vincent can tick it off. Email each person who asked for something, apart from me, to say what happened to their asks. When it's done tell me here how many Go, Hold and Drop.
quotes.rule: Beta message rule. A message is anything the game puts on a player's phone while the game is closed. Run these tests in order and stop at the first one that fails. 1. The feature behind it is in the beta. 2. The client can send it without a server. 3. The client already schedules it. 4. It can reach the players it is written for. A player only counts once our own permission ask has happened, the settings toggle doesn't count. It fails only if none of them count. 5. It fires on the right day. The hour doesn't matter for beta, the day does. 6. Vincent has seen it arrive on both iOS and Android. Go: it passes all six. Drop: it fails test 1, or the client already covers it under another message, then name that message. Hold: anything else, and name the test it failed. In the beta means live in Zombie Match today or on the BETA list of the ZM ROADMAP board. Neither status column on the sheet decides anything. What Vincent counts as seen is in his QA note. The permission ask is Robert's call. The final headline is the latest line I've called. A line that differs from what the client ships needs a string ticket under DES-314, because the strings are hard-coded, so open one when you make the call. Emoji don't count as a different line. Final headline and String change are only for Go rows. Audience is who the ask says it's for. Drop tickets go to Canceled, Go tickets stay as they are, Hold tickets go back to Todo unless the roadmap says otherwise.
quotes.qa: How I'm checking the phone messages for beta. Seen only counts on a store build, on a real iOS device and a real Android device. A build with shortened timers doesn't count, it only proves the code path. Moving the phone date forward on a store build is fine.
quotes.ask_decision: Permission ask for beta: leaving our own ask after level 20, not pushing it further, Leonard's right that we need PNs for retention. The Unity popup at launch on iOS stays as it is.
quotes.ask_reply: that popup doesn't switch anything on btw. NotificationManager only schedules once our own ask has run or they switch it on from settings, on both platforms

quotes.ladder_review: Cancelled, no need. The weekly one repeats for four weeks, so day 14 is already covered.
